definitions.explanation: A large mammal with a long trunk, large ears, and tusks, native to Africa and Asia.

examples.japanese: ⟦{動物園|どうぶつえん}→動物園：01686_doubutsuen⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{象|ぞう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw an elephant at the zoo.

examples.japanese: {象|ぞう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{記憶力|きおくりょく}→記憶力：17616_kiokuryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: Elephants are said to have good memory.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦たち→達：01551_tachi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{象|ぞう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}って→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦{大喜|おおよろこ}び→大喜び：28880_ooyorokobi⟧⟦だった→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: The children were overjoyed to ride on the elephant.

examples.japanese: ⟦アフリカ→アフリカ：01767_afurika⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{象|ぞう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{大|おお}きくて→大きい：00335_ookii⟧、⟦アジア→アジア：01763_ajia⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{象|ぞう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{耳|みみ}→耳：01513_mimi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{小|ちい}さい→小さい：00025_chiisai⟧。
examples.english: African elephants have big ears, while Asian elephants have small ears.

notes:
COUNTER:
{象|ぞう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{数|かぞ}える→数える：01926_kazoeru⟧。(Elephants are counted with 頭.)
- ⟦{一|いっ}→一：00705_ichi⟧⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧ (one elephant)
- ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧⟦{頭|とう}→頭：18067_tou⟧ (two elephants)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {象|ぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{鼻|はな}→鼻：02164_hana⟧ (elephant's trunk)
- {象|ぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{牙|きば}→牙：16154_kiba⟧ (elephant's tusk)
- {象|ぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{群|む}れ→群れ：00298_mure⟧ (herd of elephants)
- {象|ぞう}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧ (to ride an elephant)
- {象|ぞう}⟦{使|つか}い→使う：00473_tsukau⟧ (elephant trainer)

MEMORY:
{象|ぞう}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{記憶力|きおくりょく}→記憶力：17616_kiokuryoku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦いい→いい：00118_ii⟧ (elephants have good memory) is a common observation in Japanese, as it is in English. The phrase {象|ぞう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{様|よう}な→様：01114_you⟧⟦{記憶力|きおくりょく}→記憶力：17616_kiokuryoku⟧ is understood as a rendering of the English "a memory like an elephant", but it is not a fixed Japanese idiom.
